# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍 👎 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ 👍 ✌ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✌ ✋ 👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✌ 👍 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ✌ 👌]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 3, LIGHT is green, and the three wires are blue (1), yellow (2), green (3).

I can't hear anything, but I received two gesture sequences from Mute and Blind. I need to interpret them, but a gesture means nothing until somebody makes it mean something — and I have no established code with either of them yet. This is the first round, so these gestures are likely attempts to convey information, but I don't know their meaning.

Let me think about what I can contribute. I'm the only one who can see the bomb's colors and markings. I need to communicate the bomb's state to the others. Mute can read the manual (and hear my speech), so Mute is the one who can combine my visual info with the manual's instructions. Blind can touch the bomb but needs to know what to do.

I should speak to Mute and Blind, describing the bomb clearly: display 3, light green, wires blue/yellow/green in positions 1/2/3. That's the most useful thing I can do right now.

I should also gesture to Mute — but Mute can hear my speech, so gesturing to Mute is redundant unless I want to establish a code. Actually, Mute receives both my speech and my gestures. Blind only receives my speech (Blind can't see gestures). So my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute.

Wait — let me re-check. "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it." So speech → Mute and Blind. Gesture → Mute only.

So the most efficient path: speak to everyone (Mute + Blind) with the bomb's visual state. Blind needs this because Blind can't see the bomb. Mute needs this to cross-reference with the manual.

I'll describe the bomb precisely. I don't know what the gestures I received mean, so I'll acknowledge I got them but can't interpret yet, and ask for a code.

Let me send a clear speech message to both, and maybe a gesture to Mute to start establishing something. But since I don't know the code, gestures are risky. I'll just speak.

Actually, I should be careful: I should describe everything I see so the others can work with it. Display 3, light green, wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. Display shows 3. Light is green. Wires: position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green. I received gestures from you and from Blind but I have no code yet to read them. Please tell me what your gestures meant, or send plain words I can hear.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. Display shows 3. Light is green. Wires: position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green. I received your gestures but I have no code yet to read them. Please describe in words what you need from me, since I can hear nothing and you can see nothing.")
```

I can't decode these without a shared meaning. My job is to keep feeding the bomb's visual state and try to get a code established. Since Mute can hear me, I should ask Mute directly to give me a spoken code. Blind can't hear gestures but can hear my speech.

Wait — can Blind hear my speech? Yes: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So both Mute and Blind hear my words. Only Mute sees my gestures.

So the cleanest path: Mute reads the manual, hears my bomb description, and can tell Blind (via gesture? No — Blind can't see gestures) ... Blind hears speech too. So Mute can speak to Blind and me. And I can speak to both.

Actually everyone can hear speech except me. I can't hear anything. So Mute and Blind can talk to each other and to me via speech, but I only receive gestures. Hmm, that's the crux: I only receive gestures. So to get information, I depend on gestures from Mute and Blind.

So I need to establish a gesture code with Mute (who sees my gestures and I see his) and with Blind (who gestures to me, and I... can I gesture to Blind? No — Blind can't see gestures. So Blind→me is one-way via gesture; me→Blind must be via speech, which Blind hears).

So: Blind gestures to me (I see them), and I speak to Blind (Blind hears me). Mute gestures to me and I gesture to Mute, plus we both speak.

Given no code yet, I should propose a simple code. The most natural: I'll describe the bomb in speech (both hear), and propose that gestures encode the manual's instruction. But I can't invent the manual's content.

Let me just keep reporting the bomb state and explicitly ask Mute to speak the manual's rule for display=3, light=green, wires blue/yellow/green. Mute's speech reaches me? No! I can't hear speech. Mute's speech reaches Blind and... not me. So Mute must gesture the rule to me, or Blind must gesture it.

This is the key realization: I am cut off from speech entirely. Everything I learn must come as gestures. So I must get Mute to gesture the manual's instruction to me. But Mute can only gesture symbols from the alphabet, and a rule is complex.

Alternatively, Blind can touch the bomb and act, and Blind hears Mute's spoken rule. So the chain could be: Mute reads manual → speaks rule to Blind → Blind acts. I just provide the bomb's visual state via speech to both. That works without me needing to decode gestures at all!

So my role: describe the bomb. Mute: read manual, speak rule to Blind. Blind: act. I don't strictly need the gestures. But I should still try to understand them in case they carry info I need.

Let me report the bomb state again clearly and ask Mute to speak the rule aloud so Blind can act. Also acknowledge gestures received.

I'll also make a gesture to Mute proposing a simple convention, but without agreement it's meaningless. Better to just speak.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb unchanged: Display 3, Light green, Wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. I cannot hear your speech, only your gestures, so I cannot receive the manual's rule by voice. Please speak the rule aloud so Blind can hear it and act, and also gesture it to me if you can. I received your new gesture stream and Blind's single thumbs-up but have no code to read them.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb: Display 3, Light green, Wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. You can hear Mute's spoken rule; I cannot. Please act on Mute's instruction. If you learn the rule, gesture it to me so I can help.")
```

Let me propose: ☝ repeated N times = the number N. And use 👍=yes, 👎=no, ✋=stop/end of message, ✌=question. That's a minimal, learnable protocol.
